shortDescription: Portugal's budget surplus fell 88% to €282 million ($328 million) in the first seven months compared to a year earlier, on hefty hospital debt repayments and a surge in public investment, but reversed the first-half deficit, official data showed.($1 = 0.8610 euros)

children: Portugal's budget surplus fell 88% to €282 million ($328 million) in the first seven months compared to a year earlier, on hefty hospital debt repayments and a surge in public investment, but reversed the first-half deficit, official data showed.

The Finance Ministry's budget body said late on Monday that total revenue rose 7.4% year-on-year to €76.538 billion between January and July, while total expenditure increased at a faster pace of 10.6% to €76.256 billion.

Expenditure rose mainly due to €1.4 billion in repayments of overdue hospital debt in the first seven months, up from €167 million a year earlier, and a 40% jump in public investment to €5.6 billion in housing and rail projects.
Payments of overdue hospital debts are significantly higher this year because the government decided to settle outstanding liabilities.

It said in a statement that revenue growth was driven by tax revenue, which rose 4.2% to €41.4 billion and helped improve the overall budget position from a deficit of €213 million in the first half of the year.
The ministry said value-added tax revenue rose 6.8% on stronger economic activity and personal income tax revenue increased 5.9%.
Social security contributions climbed 6.7% to €20.8 billion, supported by a buoyant labour market, with unemployment near record lows.

Portugal's economy grew 0.8% in the second quarter from the previous three months, up from 0.1% in the first quarter, driven by net exports and private consumption, while annual growth accelerated to 2.5%, INE said.
The government expects a balanced budget this year, with neither a deficit nor a surplus, compared with a surplus of 0.7% in 2025.
